title: Optimality of the Half-Order Exponent in the Turing-Good Identities for Bayes Factors
summary: Bayes factors are widely computed by Monte Carlo, yet heavy-tailed sampling distributions can make numerical validation unreliable. The Turing--Good identities provide exact moment equalities for powers of a Bayes factor (a density ratio). When these identities are used as Good-check diagnostics, the power choice becomes a statistical design parameter.
